title: Metering policy simulator and rollback playbook for late-arrival credits
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Late-arriving usage events and downstream reconciliation jobs occasionally inject retroactive credits that meaningfully change per-tenant billed tokens. This leads to billing surprises and noisy chargeback events for customers and increases support load when automated true-ups run during invoicing windows.

Goal: Build a simulation harness that replays historical event streams and applies proposed metering policy changes (prefix-hold windows, confidence thresholds, and stochastic imputation strategies) to estimate net invoice deltas and the tail distribution of customer-facing adjustments. In parallel, author a clear rollback and remediation playbook that operators can run when a rollout generates >X% unexpected credits or >Y of high-value customer impacts.

Scope:
- A dry-run simulator service that consumes historical Kafka topic snapshots and local test corpora and produces per-tenant delta reports.
- A small web UI or CLI to run scenarios and export CSVs for finance/CS review.
- An automated test suite that validates consistency between simulator output and production reconciler on a 7-day window.
- A documented operator playbook with step-by-step rollback, customer notification templates, and reconciliation checkpoints.

Non-goals: Not building a permanent UI in Console for this iteration; not changing live billing logic without follow-up approvals and regulator sign-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay one week of Kafka topic snapshots and output per-tenant token deltas broken down by route and model variant
Simulator reports correlate with production reconciler within +/- 1% token difference for 90% of tenants on a sample week
Runbook contains stepwise rollback instructions, including feature-flag toggles, data backfill checkpoints, and customer communication templates
Automation for smoke detection: a CI job that runs the simulator against the latest nightly snapshot and fails if projected invoice deltas exceed configured thresholds
Operational docs and a short demo recorded for SRE/Support to run the simulator locally
notes:
Design decisions considered:
- Option A: Conservative prefix-hold window (30s) reduces noisy credits but can increase latency-sensitive cache misses.
- Option B: Confidence-based imputation (model-based) reduces credits for low-confidence matches but requires a calibrated classifier and adds complexity to audits.
We will implement both in the simulator and produce comparative reports.

Data flow for simulation: ingest kafka snapshot -> normalize events -> apply policy function -> run reconciler logic -> aggregate per-tenant deltas -> produce metrics and CSV export.

Simulator implementation notes: prototype in Python using existing replay tooling (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/usage-replay). Output schema will match production reconciliation CSV to simplify diffing.

Rollout thresholds proposed: auto-block rollout if simulator predicts >5% of tenants will see a credit >$100 or if net platform credit across the tenant population changes by >2% vs baseline. These thresholds are draft and will be reviewed with Finance.

Operational playbook outline:
1) Detect: alert fires from canary run or daily batch with simulated delta metrics
2) Triage: run targeted replay for affected tenant subset and generate forensic report
3) Mitigate: flip feature flag controlling the new policy or revert to last known-good policy via runtime-config service
4) Backfill: schedule controlled backfill job that re-runs reconciliation with last-known-good algorithm and produce provisional adjustments
5) Communicate: use template to notify impacted customers and share remediation ETA
6) Postmortem: create incident and update regression tests
implementation_plan:
Week 1: wire up replay of compressed Kafka snapshots and build base reconciler adapter. Week 2: add policy plugins (prefix-hold, confidence-impute, stochastic-smoother). Week 3: integrate CI smoke test and produce sample reports for Finance. Week 4: finalize operator playbook and demo to SRE/Support.

Testing: unit tests for each policy plugin, end-to-end replay test against synthetic dataset, and correlation tests vs production outputs.

Observability: export simulator metrics to dev-statsd and persist run artifacts to S3 for auditing. Dashboard: create temporary Grafana dashboard for scenario comparisons.
risk_and_mitigation:
Risk: Simulator outputs could diverge from production due to subtle differences in provenance headers or late-arriving event semantics. Mitigation: implement comprehensive normalization and a checksum-based provenance verifier.

Risk: Rollback playbook may require manual steps across runtime-config and job orchestration systems. Mitigation: script common steps and create a documented runbook with pre-populated commands.

Risk: Finance disagreement on thresholds. Mitigation: present multicriteria reports (absolute dollars, percent of invoices, number of customers impacted) and iterate with Finance and CS.
runbook_snippets: Backfill checklist: 1) Lock invoice window 2) run reconciler in dry-run 3) validate deltas 4) schedule monotonic backfill job with rate limiting
